findings.explanation: The cited defect is a host-specific retrieval origin, not a file placed outside the composed root. The analysis and recorded input selectors use supplied eyegaze TSVs, not that upstream acquisition source. The assessment even calls it optional. This does not establish that an essential file is outside the common root for the scoped numerical results, figures and manuscript.

Retain the unresolved nested source URL under must/002 and may/001, clearly distinguishing its optional upstream role; alternatively identify a concrete essential out-of-boundary dependency before retaining partial.

That is positive evidence of incomplete recursive linking, even though the direct study consumers use the already distributed TSVs. Partial appropriately preserves the working top-level links; it must not be described as an observed failure to retrieve those TSVs.

The delivered Dockerfile declares scientific libraries and rendering tools, while Docker-Makefile installs the independently pinned detector. The native equivalent-evidence rule accepts package declarations and does not require physical vendoring. Version exactness is a separate criterion.

The frozen inventory supplies Git identities for analysis code, manuscript, configuration and figures, and the cached Git tree confirms the module commits. Capture omissions cannot demonstrate untracked source files. The assessment correctly avoids equating a logistical checkout's missing paths with lack of version control.

The root inventory contains annex symlinks and content keys for the large image layers; the raw-data README describes Git-annex content management separately from Git metadata. These establish versioned binary identity without requiring the deliberately omitted payload bytes.

The 2023 completed record names container/image as an input and img plus results_def.tex as outputs; its parent tree contains the saved image and detector pin. By contrast, root > label dataset > bdcde2 records bash code/compute_all.sh without an exact environment. That real provenance difference supports partial. This does not certify that every shipped derivative was inspected byte-for-byte.

The README provides installation, cloning, numerical rerun and manuscript commands. The container Makefile and registration implement those commands. The legacy route is explicitly labelled old, so its coexistence does not trigger the native silent-conflict rule.

The named results-containerized tag resolves locally to the cited completed analysis commit. The separate main.pdf target is also implemented through docker-make. This is concrete entry-point evidence; a new execution is unnecessary to establish a clear starting point.

The root analysis constructs data paths under the root and the Docker cleanup targets are internal image paths. The linked label submission script does embed a particular home directory and executable location. Partial is supported for the declared linked-code boundary, provided the legacy nature remains explicit.

Inspection of the current analysis imports, local test utilities, detector imports and manuscript Makefiles found corresponding declared Python/rendering packages or base-system tools. DataLad has an explicit fallback inside the image and is supplied on the host to provision inputs. This supports the assessment's source-level dependency conclusion for the documented current route, not an observed image installation or a claim about all optional upstream utilities.

The root identifies host tools, tested operating systems and Docker compatibility, and registration explains its mount and HOME handling. Root > label dataset still documents a Condor workflow whose script embeds a particular deployment directory. That narrower undisclosed host assumption is concrete enough for partial; it is not a defect inferred from a Docker-internal absolute path.

The root requirements list is clear. In the explicitly linked label component, README directs readers to obsolete preprocessing and detection programs absent from its tracked inventory, while the retained compute_all.sh uses a different route. Partial accurately captures the inconsistent component-level requirements account.

The Dockerfile and container registration are Git blobs in the assessed tree alongside the code and data links. This criterion asks whether specifications are tracked, not whether they completely freeze every upstream environment; the latter remains a valid gap elsewhere.

The build command is declared in bdac0e1, a subsequent tracked Dockerfile revision changes the environment configuration, and a completed image-build record follows. The later OCI conversion also has an explicit recorded command and output. Under the native rule accepting a runnable declaration plus tracked instances, met is defensible. The identical answer and upstream-duplicate flag for must/014 and should/008 are consistent.

The archive is identified by config/layer content and the adapter executes the computed image ID, so its latest label is not evidence of a floating runtime image. The upstream label execution has no exact environment identity. Partial gives appropriate credit to the archived root environment while retaining that gap.

Public clone instructions and advertised annex locations do not prove independent access to image and input payloads at the assessed revision. The frozen cohort forbids the necessary retrieval test. Not-checked is correctly separated from a failed retrieval and from the positive archival-design findings.

The current README explains obtaining DataLad, its container extension and Docker, then cloning and executing the named container route. Registration points to an actual archived image layout. The instructions have a mechanism behind them, and the historical route is clearly disclosed.

The discovered code and data modules use Git identities; DataLad and annex extend those Git-based records for payloads. Independent repository histories do not constitute incompatible version-control systems.

A completed root analysis and later image maintenance are observable, but neither establishes a regular test schedule for the documented study workflow. The detector's Travis job tests a package, not the paper instructions. Not-checked is preferable to asserting that no manual repeated testing exists.

The root separates acquired data, label derivatives, reusable software, study analysis, figures and container definition through named modules and directories. The native property-based interpretation does not require every directory to be a separate repository.

The image build and subsequent exit-zero analysis are completed historical records, and the README-linked adapter creates a new docker run --rm instance. Together they meet the native allowance for equivalent completed fresh-run evidence. The conclusion concerns historical root pipeline execution, not a fresh reviewer replay, current accessibility or numerical validation.

The root mechanism creates and removes a container per invocation. The linked label-generation command delegates directly to caller Python and defines no disposable environment. Partial is warranted for workflow design across those components; the record alone should not be taken to prove that the historical caller machine was long-lived.

The 2025 conversion exercises loading and running exit 0, but does not repeat the numerical/manuscript computation; the package CI also does not reconstruct the exact archived study environment. This evidence does not settle regular environment reconstitution testing. The cautious unknown is supported.

The saved image is represented inside the research object by manifests and annexed config/layer objects, backed by a completed save record. That establishes archived environment artifacts rather than merely a registry name. Current recipient retrieval remains separately unverified under must/016.

The build command is declared in bdac0e1, a subsequent tracked Dockerfile revision changes the environment configuration, and a completed image-build record follows. The later OCI conversion also has an explicit recorded command and output. Under the native rule accepting a runnable declaration plus tracked instances, met is defensible. The raw-data documentation explicitly states unrestricted access, and the inspected study acquisition route identifies no restricted component. Treating the empty restricted-component subject as not-applicable follows the native rule. This is not a test of current server access.

The independently maintained detector and datasets have explicit repository boundaries and Git pins, including nested evaluation data. The local-only lab-eyetracking URL prevents a clean positive for all linked components. This reasoning concerns project components rather than incorrectly demanding submodules for ordinary Python packages.

The root documentation explains the overall reproduction route and module configuration supplies a navigable component list, but the linked label README describes an obsolete composition rather than compute_all.sh. The discrepancy is a concrete limitation on explaining relationships and recombination, supporting partial without insisting on a particular diagram format.

The cited source confirms use of detector test utilities, fixed data paths and event columns. Those facts show interface dependencies, but do not by themselves establish that independent compatible module updates break the workflow. Different detector pins can instead demonstrate independent component versioning; the label history explicitly records an independent detector update. No concrete incompatible boundary change or required cross-module edit is identified.
findings.suggested_correction: Distinguish normal declared input contracts from an actual modularity defect. Cite a specific boundary violation or compatible update that requires coordinated edits before retaining partial; otherwise qualify this as an unverified coupling risk and revisit the status rather than treating arbitrary replacement compatibility as the criterion.

findings.explanation: Submodule links compose independently versioned inputs and software; the container registration and completed run record connect the image, commands, input selectors and outputs. These are explicit mechanisms for composing the object, regardless of whether every remote was accessible during review.

Navigation is supported by root usage instructions and Git module paths. Nevertheless, following the linked label README leads to missing legacy programs instead of its extant generation script. This is a specific navigation problem supporting partial; the absence of a consolidated guide alone would not suffice because the criterion also permits tooling.

limitations: Inspection only, using frozen manifest data/remodnav-evidence.json with SHA256 e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. No network, payload acquisition, container build, scientific execution or new replay occurred.

Binary/annex payloads and container layers were intentionally omitted. Their current retrievability, byte integrity and scientific outputs were not independently tested. Public citation contents were checked against frozen source/history, not live services.

Only the assigned anonymized assessment was read. Its original probe receipt and human report were outside the permitted review input, so claims about exact probe behavior and report presentation were not independently audited. Source-level conclusions were checked independently; all 31 native answers passed validation, which does not establish substantive correctness.

All 267 manifest-listed source/history hashes were checked without mismatch. Available cached Git trees and tag resolution were read with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. Some other historical blobs are absent; no attempt was made to acquire them.

The supplied response has 17 MUST answers (9 met, 7 partial, 1 not-checked), 9 SHOULD answers (5 met, 1 partial, 2 not-checked, 1 not-applicable), and 5 MAY answers (1 met, 4 partial). No aggregate score or contradictory denominator appears in the assigned JSON; report-level denominator presentation could not be reviewed.

The review distinguishes current study reproduction from optional upstream acquisition and legacy linked scripts. The common-root disagreement and modular-update evidence request are judgment findings, not demonstrated runtime failures. Agreement is not human approval.
